head: 0a3bb5fb716120b452a4fccf4ef36926c2c429c5
summary: I built both tools the design called for. eng/rules-parity.ps1 is a dependency-free PowerShell check that runs under both 5.1 and 7. It reads ArchitectureRulesTests.cs and the twinned fitness.yaml entries above the first '# settled by' marker, applies the closed normaliser ((?m) required, then stripped; the three BOM-guard spellings read as '^'), pairs Facts and entries by pattern multiset, and refuses (exit 2) any shape it cannot classify. RuleCopiesAgreeTests.cs is its only permanent caller: it counts Facts by reflection and launches powershell.exe. eng/rules-harness/harness.py is the SL-022 harness, ported. It imports the real taad3.fitness from a required --engine-root, builds one scratch copy with the repo's SDK, and judges 19 plant rows and 13 divergence rows against the recorded outcomes, restoring each batch against SHA-256 hashes. On the real tree it gives CLEAN (17 rules, 7 Facts) and 32/32 AS-RECORDED, identical across three runs. tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 feeds each of the 14 case shapes in. For each guard it also puts the defect back and checks that the guard catches it: a yaml typo fails the Fact, a deleted scope gives MISSED-BY-*, a moved exempt plant gives FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT, and a flipped row gives DIVERGENCE-CLOSED. All 14 cases pass, and Core.Tests passes 120/120.

files.why: C3/C4: the text parity check. Exits 0 AGREE, 1 DRIFT (names the unpaired entry or Fact with file:line and the nearest one on the other side), 2 CANNOT-READ. Includes a self-mutation test and the -ExpectFacts guard. All comparisons are ordinal and all output is ASCII.

The single async Fact. It counts ArchitectureRulesTests Facts by reflection, launches powershell.exe on the parity script with -ExpectFacts, and asserts exit 0 with the script's output in the message. It parses nothing, and its name leaves out 'ArchitectureRulesTests'.

C1/C2: port of SL-022's setup3/analyse3, divergences.ps1 and encodings.ps1. Engine imported from a required --engine-root, with TAAD3_HOME and dont_write_bytecode set before the import. Runs parity first, then a scratch copy (git ls-files -co) built once, a clean baseline, and batched rows with hash-checked restores. Verdicts: AS-RECORDED, MISSED-BY-*, FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT, DIVERGENCE-CLOSED, STRAY-HIT, PLANT-BROKEN. It also checks that git status is unchanged.

19 rows: F01-F16 are the 16 must-fire hits from SL-022's final validation, with one plant per scope of each split Fact. P07c-P07e are the exempt-file rows. The _note reconciles 16 against 17 (14 must-fire + 3 exempt, all 14 shapes covered).
D1-D12 are the 12 recorded disagreements from SL-022's three outputs, as strict rows. D13 (cp1252) was measured by SL-031 and is pinned as an agreement.

Case runner (C-001 to C-014), in the pattern of tests/window/WindowCases.ps1. Parity shapes run under powershell.exe and pwsh; harness shapes run against the real engine. Each guard's bite is shown on %TEMP% copies.

Comment-only header edit. The header now names eng/rules-parity.ps1, RuleCopiesAgreeTests and eng/rules-harness/harness.py, says where twinned entries go, and tags the divergence list with D1-D13. The three '# settled by SL-031' entries at the end were already in the tree before this build (the engine appended them at design).
One comment line above the class: one verbatim literal per pattern line, read by eng/rules-parity.ps1. No behaviour change.

obligations.how: RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 runs rules-parity.ps1 on the real tree under powershell.exe 5.1 and pwsh 7, with and without -ExpectFacts 7. It asserts exit 0 and 'AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns; 7 settled entries' (7 settled, not 4: the 3 SL-031 rules the engine appended). 8/8 checks pass. The Fact RuleCopiesAgreeTests also passes on the tree.

C-002 feeds four shapes under both shells: a yaml typo in one scope entry of a split Fact, a typo in a one-scope Fact's twin, one of five patterns dropped from C#, and one dropped from yaml. Each gives exit 1, names the entry and the Fact with file:line, and shows the differing patterns. 34/34 checks pass. Separately, a yaml typo in a scratch copy fails RuleCopiesAgreeTests.

C-003 checks four shapes. A one-scope twin deleted: the Fact pairs with nothing. A split Fact changed: both stale entries and the Fact are reported ('DRIFT 3'). A new entry above the marker: the entry pairs with no Fact. The same entry appended below a '# settled by' marker: AGREE with 8 settled. 26/26 checks pass.

C-004 checks four things. A twinned pattern without (?m) is DRIFT, with the output saying it lacks (?m). The BOM guard written as ﻿, ﻿, ﻿ and a literal U+FEFF all read AGREE. ﻿ without '?' is DRIFT. All under both shells; 26/26 checks pass.

C-005 covers these shapes: two literals on one C# line, concatenation, raw string, const, nameof, interpolated string, a Fact with no AssertNoMatch, a Fact with zero patterns, zero Facts, -ExpectFacts 8, and double-quoted, block and plain yaml patterns. Each gives exit 2 with CANNOT-READ and the exact file:line under both shells; 54/54 checks pass.

C-006 covers five shapes. A nonexistent engine root and a root with no taad3 (the repo itself) exit 2 naming the path. So does a missing --engine-root (argparse). So does a fake engine whose check() result lacks 'unran'; its import also refuses any TAAD3_HOME other than the harness's own fsa-rules-*\home, which proves TAAD3_HOME is set before the import. So does an engine whose import raises. None is reported as a disagreement. 17/17 checks pass.

C-007 runs --scenario clean. Exit 0: CLEAN, xunit 7 Facts, 0 hits, fitness pass with 17 rules, equal to the 10 twinned + 7 settled that parity counted, and none unmatched or unran. The bite: a repo copy with a stray DllImport line in Scanner.cs exits 2 with 'the clean baseline is not clean' naming the rule and file.

C-008 runs F01-F16: 16 rows, 16 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray. The insert-after rows land at anchor lines in existing files, and F03 also fires the SL-024 NoBcl rule as recorded. Two bites, each on a copy: deleting 'InteropLivesOnlyInNative (tests)' from yaml leaves parity at AGREE (its blind spot) and gives F12 MISSED-BY-FITNESS; dropping the tests scope from the xUnit Fact gives F12 MISSED-BY-XUNIT.

C-009 runs P07c-P07e: 3 AS-RECORDED (quiet in both engines). Moving P07d into non-exempt DirectoryReader.cs gives FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT, exit 1. Dropping EntryClassifier.cs from the yaml except_files fails the clean baseline (exit 2), because the exempted file really holds the forbidden text.
C-010 runs D1 (packages/) and D2 (dist/). Both AS-RECORDED: xUnit fires, Fitness is quiet; exit 0.

C-011 runs D6 (UTF-16LE), D7 (UTF-8 over 2 MB), D10 (over 2 MB, interop), D11 (UTF-16LE under tests/) and D13 (cp1252). D6/D7/D10/D11: xUnit fires, Fitness is quiet. D13: both fire. All AS-RECORDED; exit 0.

C-012 runs D3 (EntryClassifier.cs to Entryclassifier.cs), D4 (TestNative.cs to testNative.cs) and D9 (to Testnative.cs). Each is a two-step rename through a temp name, and the harness checks the folder listing shows the new case and not the old before trusting the row. All AS-RECORDED (xUnit fires, Fitness quiet). The bite: a 'rename' to the same name is PLANT-BROKEN, exit 1.
C-013 runs D5: 'using' and 'System.Windows;' split over two lines in Scanner.cs. xUnit is quiet and Fitness fires; AS-RECORDED, exit 0.
C-014 records D13 (which both engines fire on) as fitness 'quiet' in a temp rows file. The harness exits 1 with DIVERGENCE-CLOSED and 'delete row D13 from divergences.json and its D-id ...'.

Owed to validate-slice, but the build did what it asks. The full harness (all 32 rows, divergences included) ran three times with the same verdict for every row (exit 0 each time); two runs were compared line by line: identical. Validate should re-run it.

Owed to validate-slice. Planting._rename does the two-step rename, then checks os.listdir shows the new-case name and not the old one; otherwise the row is PLANT-BROKEN. D3/D4/D9 pass that check on %TEMP% (NTFS), and C-012's bite shows a non-case rename is refused.

Owed to validate-slice. C-014 flips D13's recorded outcome in a temp rows file, and the harness exits 1 with DIVERGENCE-CLOSED. A closed divergence is caught by the exit code, not by someone reading the output.

tests.command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/rules-parity.ps1 ; pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/rules-parity.ps1 -ExpectFacts 7
tests.note: Both shells: 'rules-parity: AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns; 7 settled entries not compared', exit 0. Re-run after the yaml header edit: same.
CLEAN: xunit 7 Facts, 0 hits; fitness pass, 17 rules, 43 files read, none unmatched or unran. Scratch built in 6 s. Engine python = %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe.

All scenarios: 32 rows, 32 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray, exit 0. Ran three times (once before the header edit, twice after), same verdict for every row each time; the last two compared line by line: identical.

The first run failed. My replace_all turned Show-Name into a self-call ('call depth overflow'). Once that was fixed, C-002 named the wrong nearest Fact, C-004 said 'the same patterns' under pwsh, and C-004's setup threw. Causes: the nearest-Fact heuristic tied when no pattern was shared; pwsh 7's culture-aware -ceq treats a U+0001-prefixed string as equal; and the file tools had turned my '﻿' escapes into real U+FEFF characters. Fixed with a tie-break, ordinal comparison, and escapes built from [char]92 / chr(0xFEFF).

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (and C-002, C-003, C-004, C-005)
tests.note: After the fixes: C-001 8/8, C-002 34/34, C-003 26/26, C-004 26/26, C-005 54/54 checks, each under both powershell.exe and pwsh.
C-006 17/17 (re-run after tightening the fake engine's TAAD3_HOME check). C-007 9/9, including the stray-violation bite (exit 2).

C-008: 16/16 AS-RECORDED; the scope-deleted-from-yaml bite gives MISSED-BY-FITNESS and the xUnit-scope bite gives MISSED-BY-XUNIT. C-009: P07c-e AS-RECORDED; FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT bite; the dropped-exemption bite exits 2.
C-010 4/4, C-011 7/7, C-012 8/8 (includes the PLANT-BROKEN bite), C-013 3/3, C-014 5/5 (DIVERGENCE-CLOSED, exit 1).
8/8. The first build gave 4 xUnit1031 warnings (blocking .Result); the Fact was made async, and the re-run passes 8/8 with no warnings.

tests.command: eng/dotnet.ps1 test <%TEMP% copy>/tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~RuleCopiesAgreeTests (yaml typo AttributesToSkip -> AttributesToSkp)
tests.note: Failure was the expected result: this proves the Fact bites. Failed 1 with 'rules-parity: DRIFT 2 unpaired', naming the Fact at ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:40 and the entry at fitness.yaml:118. The copy was deleted afterwards.
Full suite with the default filter: Passed 120, Failed 0, Skipped 0.

tests.command: <engine python> eng/rules-harness/harness.py --engine-root ... --scenario divergences --only D12 --divergences <temp copy with lines.fitness=2>
tests.note: Failure was the expected result: an ad-hoc check that D12's line-offset pin is not vacuous. Exit 1, MISSED-BY-FITNESS, 'fitness fired at planted-line offset [1], recorded 2'. Temp dirs removed.

deviations: The harness takes --engine-root as required with no TAAD3_BACKEND env fallback. The design said '--engine-root E | env TAAD3_BACKEND', but O-004's disposition (newer) says required, with no default.

The harness has options the design did not name: --dotnet-from, --scenario, --only, --plants and --divergences. The case tests need them to feed one shape at a time and to build mutated %TEMP% copies with this repo's SDK without a 300 MB download per copy. With no options, the behaviour is the design's. The harness also probes the engine (import plus result fields, on a tree holding only fitness.yaml) before running parity, so an unreachable engine fails before anything costs a build. Both cases exit 2.

Added tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, which the design does not list. The case obligations need a runnable command that feeds each shape, and the repo's precedent is tests/window/WindowCases.ps1. The bite tests run the harness on %TEMP% copies given a throwaway `git init`, because the harness copies what git lists. This repo's version-control state is not touched.

The settled count is 7, not the design's and criterion's 4, and the clean Fitness rule count is 17, not 14. The engine appended SL-031's own three architecture_rules under '# settled by SL-031' at design time. The design's derivation (twinned + settled) holds; only its numbers were stale.

Row schema extensions: 'also' (extra rules one planted line fires: F03 also fires the SL-024 NoBcl rule, and D1/D2 fire two Facts), 'lines' (the per-engine planted-line offset, needed for D12, whose recorded divergence is only the reported line), 'to' (the rename-case target), 'encoding'/'pad_to_bytes' allowed on new-file too, and 'note'. The row files are {_note, rows}.

The design wanted a cp1252 divergence row (C-011) with a 'recorded per-engine outcome', but SL-022 never recorded cp1252, and the design's premise that it is read differently is wrong. Measured: both engines read a single-byte file as UTF-8 with replacement and both fire. D13 pins that as an agreement row, not a divergence, and the header now says so.

Build order: I did not copy the raw %TEMP% SL-022 sources into the worktree first. I read all 15 files while they were present and ported them directly. Copied raw under eng/, they would break the new 'eng tooling carries no machine-specific path' rule (they hard-code C:\Users\... and sl022-* paths).

Plant ids: must-fire rows are F01-F16, because setup3 had no ids. The exempt rows keep SL-022's P07c-P07e as the design names them. setup3's '#if PLANTED' wrappers and its Compile Remove line were dropped, because the harness runs --no-build. D12 keeps '#if PLANTED' because its blank-line shape needs a non-blank line before it.
not_built: The TAAD3_BACKEND environment fallback for the engine root, dropped per O-004 (see deviations).
The optional switch of run_fitness() to a taad_v3 CLI. The design said the build 'may'. In-process import through one adapter function was kept.
follow_ups: No plant or exemption row covers FileSystemCallsGoThroughTheCancelGuard (SL-024) or its except_files (Kernel32.cs, SynchronousIoCancel.cs). TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls is covered only through F03's 'also'. A scope or exemption drift on those rules is invisible to both tools until a person adds rows with measured outcomes.
The 7 settled entries (SL-023, SL-024, SL-031) have no behavioural coverage and no xUnit twin. The harness only confirms they are clean and matched on the real tree.

The engine's file-writing tools turn a '\uXXXX' sequence in written content into the character itself: '﻿' was stored as U+FEFF in three files before I caught it. Anyone editing the BOM-guard lines of .taad/fitness.yaml, or writing such escapes through those tools, needs [char]92 or chr() constructions. Worth fixing in the engine.

The design-slice open questions are still for a person. Should the parity Fact run on every `dotnet test` (it does now; deleting RuleCopiesAgreeTests.cs reverses it)? Is a harness that runs only where the taad_v3 checkout exists acceptable?

pwsh 7's -eq/-ceq on strings compares by culture and ignores ICU-ignorable characters such as U+0001 and U+FEFF. Any other repo PowerShell that compares pattern or path text with -ceq could hide a difference, so an audit may be worthwhile.
